A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 27-page NaLA study, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the research content is identical; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v1 reports original layout-generation experiments, AI and human evaluations, efficiency measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including baseline comparisons, human evaluations, and appendix backbone ablations.

M1.justification: The point-cloud encoders, Q-Formers, coarse-to-fine pose prediction, training objective, and staged training procedure are identical in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions use 3D-FRONT and Imaginarium and retain the same room categories, irregular-room scenarios, and appendix examples. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Both compare against LayoutGPT, Holodeck, and LayoutVLM in Table 1, DirectLayout in Table 5, and LayoutGPT alone in the irregular-room comparison.

E3.justification: The asset splits, training budgets, model configurations, evaluation metrics, and judging procedures are identical. Both retain three test cases per each of 20 scene categories and 20 irregular-room test cases.

E4.justification: The input, output-representation, grid-resolution, augmentation, training-strategy, and backbone ablations are unchanged. The irregular-scene evaluation and Appendix E failure cases also match.

E5.justification: Both report standard errors using 1,000 bootstrap resamples in Table 1 and average efficiency measurements over five repetitions in Appendix D.5. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and graphical and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains NaLA's overall AI score of 3.53 and human score of 3.69.

T1.justification: The problem assumptions, loss, pose-discretization and reconstruction equations, and metric definitions are identical, including Appendices B and D.3. No mathematical reasoning is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion make identical claims about native geometric perception, coarse-to-fine placement, layout quality, and inference efficiency.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same limitations concerning scarce training data, rare assets, backbone capability, and placement failures.

D1.justification: Architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, evaluation prompts, and the project-page link are unchanged. The updated arXiv self-link introduces no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements, and all 41 references are identical. No cited work or relationship to prior methods changes.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 28 Jun 2026, to v2, 13 Aug 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–6, captions, and body layout are unchanged. Pages 2–27 render identically, and the first-page body also matches; the stamp update is the text edit recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, reproducibility details, and appendices are identical. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's quality.
